name: Vaccine recalls
instructions: Read overdue_patients.csv. List every patient overdue for rabies or DHPP, sorted by days overdue (most overdue first). For each owner draft a short reminder text using the pet's name and the booking link from the reminder policy. Skip Biscuit and the Whitfield family entirely. Anything for Elm St. Rescue waits for Kayla's sign-off.

name: No-show rebooking
instructions:
1. When someone texts that they can't make a shift, find the site, shift time and crew in the crew schedule.
2. Rank who can cover: not already scheduled then, closest to the site, and not over their hours this week.
3. Draft the text asking the top pick to cover, with a backup, and a heads-up to the crew lead.
4. Request approval from Kayla before any text goes to a cleaner or crew lead.
5. Send Kayla one short summary: who called out, who is covering, and the hours it adds.
6. Hard rules from the call, in every draft: “Never quote a price for surgery or dental work.” “Never contact the Whitfield family about Biscuit.”

Why this matters: On the call: “That's maybe two hours a week, mostly Tuesdays and Wednesdays.” — about 2 hours a week by hand today.

name: Post-surgery check-ins
instructions:
1. Collect what is needed for honestly my week from the knowledge base and memory.
2. Do the honestly my week work the way Kayla does it today (see the call notes in the knowledge base), and mark any assumption clearly.
3. Deliver the result as one document with a table (item, what was done, what needs Kayla) at the top.
4. Request approval from Kayla before anything leaves the business.
5. Hard rules from the call, in every draft: “Never quote a price for surgery or dental work.” “Never contact the Whitfield family about Biscuit.”

Why this matters: On the call: “We do eight to ten surgeries a week, so that's around three hours a week, every morning.” — about 21 hours a week by hand today.

name: Insurance claim form prep
instructions:
1. List orders/jobs completed since the last run that do not have an invoice yet.
2. Draft each invoice (customer, line items, quantities, prices, tax, terms) from the order and the price list.
3. List invoices that are past due, with days outstanding, and draft a polite reminder for each.
4. Deliver a document: invoices ready to send (table with totals), reminders drafted, and anything that needs the owner.
5. Request approval from Kayla before any invoice or reminder is sent.
6. Hard rules from the call, in every draft: “Never quote a price for surgery or dental work.” “Never contact the Whitfield family about Biscuit.”

Why this matters: On the call: “Owners send us the form, I fill in the medical history and the invoice codes.” — about 4 hours a week by hand today.

name: Review requests & responses
instructions:
1. List patients whose visit or job finished today and draft a short review request for each.
2. Draft responses to new reviews (thank positive ones by name; offer to make negative ones right, offline).
3. Request approval from Kayla before any request or response is sent.
4. Hard rules from the call, in every draft: “Never quote a price for surgery or dental work.” “Never contact the Whitfield family about Biscuit.”

Why this matters: On the call: “Google reviews come in, I try to answer them, about an hour and a half a week, usually Sunday night.” — about 1.5 hours a week by hand today.
